pill.desc: clear, colorless solution in a single-dose glass vial

tell: An intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide with a plasma half-life of 63 to 87 days and maintenance doses every 4 months.

clues.text: Metabolized by exonuclease hydrolysis rather than CYP450 enzymes, and not an inhibitor or inducer of them. Urinary excretion is the likely route, but only 0.5% of the dose is recovered in urine at 24 hours.
Supplied as the sodium salt, with 2.4 mg of active moiety per mL equivalent to 2.53 mg of the salt.
Approved under an NDA in 12, 28 and 50 mg single-dose vials, given every 14 days at first and then every 4 months.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Lower respiratory infection and constipation are the most common adverse reactions.
Spinal muscular atrophy in pediatric and adult patients.
Directed at SMN2, it increases exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 transcripts, raising production of full-length SMN protein.
The generic name begins with N and has ten letters.
